Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

scRTtools 0.0.0.9001

  • New vignette figures and 500-cell vignette data downloaded from a GitHub release (see below).
  • scrt_example_data() loads the GenomicRanges namespace, so the restored GRanges work (e.g. names()) in a fresh session.

scRTtools 0.0.0.9000

First development version: 111 exported functions for single-cell DNA replication timing analysis of 10x multiome data. Plotting code is not included.

Modules

  • Genome bins and counting: make_fixed_bins(), compute_bin_mappability(), count_reads(), filter_windows(), calculate_OE_ratio(), smooth_windows(), export_mcol().
  • Cell QC and G1 windows: calculate_mapd(), find_g1_cells(), define_G1_windows(), synchronize_bins().
  • Fragment downsampling: optimize_shrink_factor(), downsample_fragments() (wraps inst/scripts/downsample_fragments_fast.sh).
  • Replication states: infer_single_cell_states() (HMM with three Rcpp kernels), assign_replication_states(), compute_rep_percent(), evaluate_state_parameters(), rank_state_parameters().
  • Tracks: define_replication_tracks(), calc_rep_track_lengths(), calc_rep_track_gaps(), count_track_centers(), summarize_track_lengths(), fit_track_velocity_linear(), fit_track_length_models(), fit_track_velocity_ode(), predict_rep_percent().
  • Pseudobulk replication timing: calculate_pseudobulk_rt(), find_rt_peaks(), annotate_peak_scores(); the S/G1 ratio variant on per-cell CP10K, aggregate_pseudobulk_s_g1_counts(), calculate_pseudobulk_rt_g1_ratio() and export_pseudobulk_g1_ratio().
  • Initiation zones: define_initiation_zones(), calculate_firing_range(), calculate_firing_order(), predict_firing_order(), fit_all_izone_velocities(); eight adjacent-zone functions; 24 zone heterogeneity functions (usage, replication tensor, clustering, non-negative CP decomposition, epigenomic models).
  • Tempo: rep_tempo(), fit_rep_tempo(), subset_rep_tempo().
  • RNA: SC2P_gene_unit(), gex_tempo(), and 12 functions for S-phase progression markers.
  • Statistics: 11 group comparison functions; HC3 regressions (fit_ols_hc3(), fit_poisson_hc3(), combine_two_samples(), full_rank_model_matrix(), add_interaction_terms(), permute_within_bins(), make_bin()).
  • Example data: scrt_example_data() (sample scRT1, chr1-chr19, 40 cells); scrt_example_data("vignette") loads a larger set of 500 cells (not QC filtered, with RNA and a bulk Repli-seq RT track), built by data-raw/make_vignette_data.R. These data (49 MB) are downloaded on first use from the data-v1 GitHub release, checked by MD5 and cached in tools::R_user_dir("scRTtools", "cache").
  • Vignette scRTtools: the workflow end to end on the example data.
  • Vignette figures: the main figures (MAPD, QC, rep_percent, pseudobulk vs bulk RT, single-cell states, UMAP, track-length velocity, initiation zones, gene replication vs expression) recomputed with ggplot2 on the 500-cell data. Its code takes 15-35 minutes, most of it in assign_replication_states(), so the vignette is precomputed: the source is vignettes/figures.Rmd.orig, and vignettes/precompute.R knits it into the committed figures.Rmd and figures-*.png.

Design

  • Parallel functions take BPPARAM (default BiocParallel::SerialParam()).
  • All inputs are explicit arguments; no function reads a config file or a fixed project path.
  • Functions return objects and write files only when that is their purpose (export_pseudobulk_g1_ratio(file = ), downsample_fragments()).
  • Count data are passed in as objects: aggregate_pseudobulk_s_g1_counts() and export_pseudobulk_g1_ratio() take a sparse matrix or a named list of per-sample matrices (no file reading, no cache_file); export_pseudobulk_g1_ratio() takes genome_granges only as a GRanges. Likewise load_and_merge_rna_counts() takes a named list of Seurat objects or count matrices, prepare_metadata() takes meta_data only as a data.frame, and calculate_OE_ratio() takes coords_list as a named list or a function(chr) loader. No function calls readRDS() on its inputs.
  • Progress messages go through verbose, which defaults to FALSE.
  • Functions that draw random numbers take a seed argument and leave the caller’s random number state untouched.
  • Results are plain data.frames (base R and data.table; no tidyverse dependency).
  • The HMM and change-point kernels are compiled C++ (Rcpp).

Testing

  • Every module is tested on synthetic data with known answers.
  • The functions were validated against the in-house analysis code they were derived from, on synthetic data and on a 21-step chain over the example data (cell QC to HC3 regressions). These comparison tests need files that are not distributed and skip when they are missing.
